subtopic: Repurchase Pricing and Net Asset Value
source_evidence: Every three, six, or twelve months at NAV from fund. You will not know the exact price you will receive for selling your shares at the time you decide to accept the repurchase offer.
answer: Interval fund repurchases are generally offered every three, six, or twelve months, and the repurchase price is based on the fund’s net asset value (NAV). The price is set on a specified date after shareholders must accept the offer, so you will not know the exact price when you decide to accept. In short, the NAV-based price is determined later, rather than being known when you submit your acceptance.
